summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including morbid obesity, polymyositis, interstitial lung disease, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, and recurrent venous thromboembolism was admitted for worsening dyspnea and right shin pain. She reported recent non-adherence to her diuretic and diabetes medications due to work demands. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic diastolic heart failure exacerbated by fluid retention, with no evidence of pulmonary embolism on CT. She was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned back to oral torsemide. The right shin lesion was evaluated by ultrasound, showing inflammatory changes consistent with cellulitis but no abscess; she was started on oral doxycycline and cephalexin. Her INR was subtherapeutic, so warfarin was increased to 6.5 mg daily. Urine and blood cultures showed no infection. She improved clinically, was discharged home, and instructed to follow up with her heart clinic and primary care provider for medication management and monitoring.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Body mass index [BMI] 70 or greater, adult
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
